az_bivy_boulder.blurb: A small bouldering spot of six problems in the Cochise Trail Boulders group at Cochise Stronghold, southern Arizona, close to the campground. The centerpiece is a big, blank roof that leans against a pedestal, with lines up the arêtes on either side. The problems run from very easy lowball climbs through to a few serious hard ones, reaching about V7, so it suits a mellow session for beginners as well as strong boulderers. Once the main trail crosses the creek, walking up the creek bed gets you to the boulder faster than staying on the trail.

az_dam_wall.blurb: A compact trad wall in the Granite Dells near Prescott, standing out as the biggest face in the stretch downstream of the dam. It holds six routes, all trad, from an easy 5.7 up to 5.11, with a good share in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so it suits climbers comfortable placing their own gear on moderate to hard cracks and seams. The granite here is described as having a handful of quality lines, but loose rock is a real concern, so test holds and wear a helmet.

az_table_dome.blurb: A multi-pitch granite dome in Mendoza Canyon, also called the Coyote Domes, in southern Arizona, sitting west of the better-known Elephant Dome. It has six traditional lines from 5.8 to 5.10, most of them five or six pitches long. The main east face catches sun for most of the day and falls into shade late in the afternoon. The rock is mostly excellent but turns poor in places, so move carefully. This is remote backcountry climbing: the walk in follows cairns across a big slab and up a gully, and fixed rappel anchors serve for the descent.

az_warpaint.blurb: One large boulder sitting in a wash in the Equestrian Area of South Mountain, in Phoenix. All six problems are on this single block and span a wide range, from a pair of V3s through a couple of V5s up to two problems around V8, so it has something for intermediate climbers and a pair of big-name lines for strong ones. It is a short stop rather than a full day venue, best combined with other South Mountain boulders, and a few pads are the norm for the landings.
